title: Kushner's Albania and Serbia developments
summary: The core of the lead holds. Kushner-linked companies won Albanian government backing for a roughly EUR 1.4B Sazan island resort and a larger Zvernec coastal project, both still awaiting approvals while he serves as Trump's envoy. Rep. Raskin's Judiciary Democrats are probing the deals, Candace Owens has attacked them, and the Trump-branded Belgrade hotel on the former army HQ site collapsed in Dec 2025 when Serbian prosecutors charged officials with forging the paperwork that lifted its heritage protection. Two points overreach: Affinity Partners denies being the investor or developer in Zvernec, where Kushner calls himself a personal minority partner, and no Trump branding is documented in Albania. That Kushner's envoy role bought him concessions is insinuation; no proof was found.

sub_claims.statement: Kushner's Affinity Partners is pursuing a luxury resort on Albania's Sazan island and the Zvernec coast.
sub_claims.finding: On 30 Dec 2024 Albania's Strategic Investment Committee, chaired by PM Edi Rama, gave strategic-investor status for a roughly EUR 1.4B Sazan resort to Atlantic Incubation Partners LLC. Reuters and others describe that company as affiliated with Affinity. The Zvernec/Vjosa-Narta project runs through different companies. In April 2026 Albania Land Development bought the coastal land from Artur Shehu. Reuters says Albania Land Development is owned by the developer Sazan Real Estate Development and other investors, and one report calls it Qatari-owned. In June 2026 Affinity's PR agency said Affinity is neither investor nor developer and that the partners invest personally. In an Oct 2026 response to The New Yorker, Kushner called himself a minority partner focused on design, with Asher Abehsera as CEO. He said partners paid EUR 230M for the land privately and that the whole project could reach about EUR 4B. Calling it 'Affinity's' project is therefore disputed. It is accurate to call it Kushner's.

sub_claims.statement: The Albanian government granted concessions/approvals for the projects.
sub_claims.finding: On 22 Feb 2024 Parliament passed Law 21/2024, amending the 2017 Protected Areas law to allow 'strategic' tourism investment in protected areas. Critics, and a European Parliament text calling for its repeal, tie the law to the Kushner plans. The Dec 2024 strategic-investor status brings fast-track approvals, and Forbes reports a 10-year tax exemption during construction (single source). A planned joint venture would put the state's stake with the Albanian Investment Corporation and the Albanian Seaports Development Company. A June 2026 draft decision would move Sazan to the Economy Ministry's administration. The government gave Zvernec preliminary approval in spring 2026, which triggered protests. Rama's office says 'there is no definitive agreement' on Sazan. Kushner concedes approvals are incomplete. The Environment Minister reportedly told the European Commission that construction is suspended pending an environmental impact assessment. Rama said the Zvernec land transaction was suspended until ownership is clarified.

sub_claims.statement: Affinity pursued a Belgrade development on the former Yugoslav army General Staff HQ site, with Serbian government concessions.
sub_claims.finding: Affinity announced the project in 2024, and in Jan 2025 Semafor reported Dubai's Mohamed Alabbar as a partner. It was a roughly $500M scheme with a 175-room hotel and residences. Under the 2024 contract Serbia agreed to strip the site's heritage status and grant a 99-year rent-free lease, with an option to take ownership. On 7 Nov 2025 Parliament voted 130-40 for a special law declaring the project of national priority and removing its heritage protection.

sub_claims.statement: The Belgrade project collapsed amid a forgery probe.
sub_claims.finding: On 15 Dec 2025 prosecutors filed an indictment proposal against Culture Minister Nikola Selakovic and other officials, alleging they forged documents to lift the site's protection in 2024. Affinity withdrew its application within hours, saying 'meaningful projects should unite rather than divide'. The trial opened on 4 Feb 2026 with not-guilty pleas; the charges carry up to 3 years. On 15 Apr 2026 Selakovic called the case politically motivated. I found no verdict as of Nov 2026. In May 2025 President Vucic had said 'there was not any kind of forgery' and offered to pardon anyone charged. After the collapse he said Serbia lost at least EUR 750M of investment.

sub_claims.statement: The Albanian land deal also faces a forgery/anti-corruption probe.
sub_claims.finding: Albania's anti-corruption prosecutor SPAK suspects the seller, Miami-based businessman Artur Shehu, of buying the Zvernec land with illicit funds and forged ownership documents. About EUR 110M of sale proceeds was frozen in a notary account; one report gives about $128M and a separate freeze on Albania Land Development's accounts. SPAK is also reported to be examining the 2024 status changes. Per Reuters, the files allege no wrongdoing by Kushner or the investors and show no sign the investors knew of the suspicions. Shehu's lawyer denies the allegations. Villagers have contested Shehu's title since a 2013 court ruling in their favour and say they warned Kushner's side about two years ago.

sub_claims.statement: The projects need foreign-government approvals while Kushner acts as a US envoy.
sub_claims.finding: Trump named Kushner 'envoy of peace' on 19 Feb 2026 (see C15). The Albanian approvals, the land transfer and the EU-driven environmental review are all pending after that date, and Kushner acknowledged in Oct 2026 that approvals were incomplete. The Belgrade deal was negotiated in 2024-25, before the title, while Kushner was already working informally on Gaza diplomacy. It collapsed in Dec 2025, so the overlap with the formal envoy title applies to Albania only.

sub_claims.statement: Rep. Jamie Raskin's House Judiciary probe.
sub_claims.finding: Raskin, the Judiciary ranking member, wrote to Kushner and Affinity in April 2026. On 24 Aug 2026 he expanded the probe to the 'suspicious $120 million' Albanian land purchase from Shehu, demanding records of communications with Albanian and US officials and of financing and approvals, with a 7 Sep deadline. He also asked whether the conduct merits review under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. On 29 Oct 2026 he sent another letter on foreign-funded bank accounts and recusal. Raskin says Kushner answered neither of the earlier letters. These are minority letters with no subpoena power, copied to Chairman Jordan.

sub_claims.statement: Right-wing figures such as Candace Owens have criticised the Albania project.
sub_claims.finding: In June 2026 Candace Owens devoted podcast segments to attacking Ivanka Trump and Kushner over the Albania resort. She mocked Ivanka's 'spiritual' framing and linked the project to Gaza. The quotes come from secondary write-ups, not the original episodes.

The Belgrade hotel was to be Trump-branded through a Trump Organization licence. Kushner said he discussed it with Eric Trump, and it was billed as Europe's first Trump hotel. For Albania I found no Trump-brand or Trump Organization licence. The family link there runs through Kushner and Ivanka.

sub_claims.statement: Implied: Kushner's envoy role or family ties secured these government concessions.
sub_claims.finding: The timing is suggestive. Albania's 2024 law came shortly after Kushner's interest became public, Vucic lobbied personally, and both governments court Washington. But no document shows a quid pro quo or that US officials intervened. The FCPA question has only been raised by Raskin. No US agency is known to be investigating.

corrections: The brief says 'Affinity Partners is pursuing' the Zvernec resort. Affinity says it is neither investor nor developer there. Kushner says he is a personal minority partner, and the land buyer is Albania Land Development, owned by Sazan Real Estate Development and other investors.

The brief cites a 'forgery probe' only for Belgrade. Albania has one too: SPAK suspects the seller, Artur Shehu, of forged deeds, and about EUR 110M of proceeds is frozen. No allegation targets Kushner.
The '$120 million' figure is Raskin's. SPAK files put the Shehu sale at about EUR 110M, and Kushner says partners paid EUR 230M for land near Zvernec in total.
The Belgrade deal predates Kushner's formal 'envoy of peace' title (Feb 2026) and collapsed in Dec 2025.
Sazan is reported at both EUR 1.4B and $1.4B; Zvernec at about EUR 4B.
denials_and_context: Kushner (Oct 2026, responding to The New Yorker) says the land was bought privately, not from the state. He says he is a minority partner and that Albania will decide whether the project proceeds. His development group says the acquisitions were lawful.
Affinity Partners says it has no role in Zvernec. On Belgrade it said it was stepping aside 'because meaningful projects should unite rather than divide'.
PM Rama says the projects comply with Albanian and EU law and will not harm protected areas. He calls the protests politically orchestrated and says the state must remain a stakeholder in Sazan.
Selakovic and his co-defendants plead not guilty and call the case political. Vucic denied any forgery and offered pardons.
SPAK's files allege no wrongdoing by Kushner or the investors, and Shehu's lawyer denies the allegations.
The protests escalated after private guards beat protesters at Zvernec on 30 May 2026. Two security firms lost their licences, police officers were suspended, and 15 protesters face proceedings.
